subject: Atlaslytics — request for per-1M token baseline and supported model list
messages:
From: Maya Singh <maya@atlaslytics.ai>
To: sean_gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 6 May 2027 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Quick question on per-1M token rates + model compatibility

Hi Sean,

We're scoping a small pilot at Atlaslytics and evaluating hosts for text-generation and embeddings. Can you send your standard per-1M token baseline for hosted API (separate input vs. output rates if applicable) and a short list of production-ready models you recommend for a classification + summarization mix?

Two quick details that would help:
- Expected IO split for our flows: ~30% input tokens, 70% output tokens (console logs / long summaries).
- Pilot target: ~750k tokens/day (spiky), potential to grow to ~5M/day if everything looks good.

Also curious if you have simple volume discount thresholds for committed usage and whether streaming or function-calling changes the token accounting.

If you can send a one-pager or a short table today, that would be ideal.

Thanks —
Maya
Maya Singh
Head of AI Products
Atlaslytics
Attachments: Atlaslytics-Pilot-Overview.pdf (attachment stub)

From: sean_gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Singh <maya@atlaslytics.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 6 May 2027 10:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick question on per-1M token rates + model compatibility

Hi Maya — great to hear from you and congrats on getting the pilot scoped. Quick answers below and I attached our compact ratecard for reference.

Summary (hosted API, current baseline):
- gpt-redwood-1: input $0.50 / 1M tokens, output $1.10 / 1M tokens
- redwood-embed-2: embeddings $0.80 / 1M tokens
- small/fast variants (redwood-lite): input $0.20 / 1M, output $0.45 / 1M (lower quality, faster)

Notes on your questions:
- IO split: pricing is billed per-token (input vs output) so the 30/70 split you mentioned maps directly to the example costs. For a daily 750k token run on gpt-redwood-1 with 30/70 split, rough daily cost = (0.3*0.75M/1M*$0.50) + (0.7*0.75M/1M*$1.10) ≈ $0.1125 + $0.5775 ≈ $0.69/day — scaled up to monthly looks different but I can run more formal math if you want.
- Streaming & function-calling: billed the same way — tokens sent/returned count toward input/output. There's no separate streaming surcharge on hosted.
- Volume discounts / committed tiers: standard bands are 5–25M/month (5% discount), 25–100M/month (12% discount), 100M+ (custom pricing). We also offer pilot credits for qualified PoCs (I can see if we can apply that here).

Recommended models for your use case:
- Summarization + high-quality classification: gpt-redwood-1 (best balance of throughput and quality).
- Cheaper bulk generation or long summaries with latency tolerance: redwood-lite-medium.
- Embeddings for semantic search: redwood-embed-2.

I've attached: redwood-hosted-ratecard-2027Q2.pdf and a quick cost-estimate template I use. If you'd like, we can do a 30-minute call this week to walk the math and discuss a commit path — I'm free Friday 11:00–12:00PT.

Cheers,
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
sean_gallagher@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0123
Attachments: redwood-hosted-ratecard-2027q2.pdf (attachment stub); atlaslytics-poc-usage-estimates.xlsx (attachment stub)

From: Maya Singh <maya@atlaslytics.ai>
To: sean_gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 7 May 2027 08:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick question on per-1M token rates + model compatibility

Thanks Sean — helpful summary. A couple of follow-ups:

1) That per-1M example math looks low relative to our expectations — can you run the monthly projection for 750k/day and for a 5M/day scale-up on gpt-redwood-1? Include both raw cost and then cost with the 5% discount band.
2) For commitments: does the discount apply to both input+output tokens or only to one side? Is there an upfront minimum or are the discounts applied retroactively on monthly billing?
3) We're especially sensitive to cold-start latency for the summary job — do you have perf numbers for 1–2K context length on gpt-redwood-1 vs redwood-lite-medium?

If it's easier, happy to jump on the call Friday; let's do 11:00PT and include an engineering lead (Arjun) who will want the perf numbers.

Best,
Maya

On attachments: I'll share our traffic profile spreadsheet after the call.
